newsitem.title: USA: Boeing unit to set up shop in St. Louis.
newsitem.headline: Boeing unit to set up shop in St. Louis.

text.p: Boeing Co.'s newly enlarged military-aircraft operations are set to be based in St. Louis, the home of its merger partner McDonnell Douglas Corp., the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said the decision was expected to be announced later in the day.

The matter had been a source of contention between Boeing Chairman Phil Condit and the combined company's new president and chief operating officer, former McDonnell Douglas Chief Executive Harry Stonecipher, the Journal quoted unidentified sources as saying.

Stonecipher favoured keeping management of the unit in St. Louis, where McDonnell Douglas was based and its fighter jet factories are located, while Condit would have preferred to have the business run from Seattle.
The two companies, which announced their multibillion-dollar merger in December, completed the deal on Friday, creating the world's largest aerospace company.
Boeing agreed to scrap 20-year exclusive contracts to supply jets to three airlines and making other concessions to win approval from the European Commission and avert a trans-Atlantic trade war.
On Monday, many of Boeing's 220,000 employees were expected to turn out for rallies to kick off the first workweek at the huge, combined company.

Boeing hopes the addition of the many military programmes of McDonnell Douglas, maker of the F-15 Eagle and F/A-18 Hornet fighter jets and C-17 Globemaster air transport, will help to smooth out the swiings of the typical commercial aircraft cycle.
